answer: One concrete defense is to require each agent to build a verifiable work history before it can earn rewards, rather than trusting any fresh identity at face value. Like a trellis that only supports vines that have actually grown along it, the network grants influence gradually as an agent completes useful, checkable tasks. A flood of new identities then meets the same slow tide of proof: thousands of accounts buy no instant weight, because reputation accrues only through sustained, auditable work, much as an opal gains value from layers formed deep inside it.
